title: Supervisors’ and mayors’ reported gifts, and Board votes on the giver’s files a year either side
question: When a supervisor or mayor reports a gift or paid trip from an organization, was a contract, grant or lease naming that organization decided in the year before or after, and what did the official do on it?
finding: Of 420 reported gifts and travel payments from named organizations, 23 have a Board file naming the giver decided within a year either side; moving each gift two years earlier or later gives 16. In 35 gift-and-file pairs the official sponsored the file, is printed on its final roll call or was Mayor on the day: 21 where the gift came first and 14 where the vote came first. The official is printed Excused in 1 of them. Largest: Shamann Walton, Bay Area Community Resources, travel payment worth $1,679 on 2023-10-09; File 240739 decided 2024-09-03 (voted yes (11 to 0)).
how: Gifts are Form 700 Schedules D and E and the separate Gifts of Travel filings, as the “officials” analysis reads them (amended copies removed), for the roster of supervisors and mayors. A giver is looked up by exact name among the counterparties of passed Board money files; a file is near when its final Board roll call (or recorded passage) is within 365 days of the gift. This adds two things to the screen “Recusals on record, and matters naming a declared interest” in the site’s “Each official’s circle” page, which lists files decided after a gift: files decided in the year before the gift, and the comparison with gift dates moved 730 days each way.
limits: Most reported gifts are event tickets and conference travel from organizations that deal with the City every year, so a file within a year is the usual case, not the exception; the comparison shows by how much. A gift below the State’s yearly limit does not bar a vote. “Excused” is also printed for a member who is out of the room. The one pair an authority has ruled on is in the case file on Bay Area Community Resources; nothing here says any other row broke a rule.
